headline: Run 16 judged Sonnet traders: 8 from 10/17, 8 pre-registered now for 10/31. Each one is a distinct, frequent signal stream that is not an anti-edge on 5-year data, and together they cover trend, mean reversion, volume, structure/ICT, breakout and one new-information stream. All 16 form one BH family (q 0.05) judged on a single pre-registered window ending 12/26. Expected false passes are about 0.03. If one trader really nets +0.10R per trade, it passes with probability 0.71-0.78. If the AI adds no edge, which is what every lens so far shows, the most likely 12/31 result is zero passes, and that is a correct answer.

recommended_count_and_why.count: 16 judged Sonnet traders (wave 1: 8, wave 2: 8) + 3 non-judged Opus twins (N23_HA_ST, N10_HA_PSAR, F16_FIB382). Every other strategy stays a cost-free rule/shadow/signal-tracking account.
why: More traders give more chances only if each one is a new bet. After merging duplicates (9 DeepSeek nested or identical definitions, the Supertrend/Ichimoku/F16/F9/F7 clusters, N06 inside N18), dropping BH-significant anti-edges (18 cells with negative 5y gross), short-only regime bets (N20, N24) and near-silent strategies, about 16 distinct, frequent streams with non-negative 5y gross remain. A 17th-30th trader would be a twin of one already staffed (fully correlated, no new chance), an anti-edge (lower prior) or too rare to test by 12/31 (power about 0).

The BH cost of size is small but real. The rank-1 threshold is p <= 0.05/K: K 12 -> 0.0042 (z 2.64), 16 -> 0.0031 (z 2.73), 24 -> 0.0021 (z 2.87), 30 -> 0.0017 (z 2.94). In sel/sim.py (two-stage design verdict, rho 0.3), the chance that one true trader (gross 0.25 over the coin flip, net about +0.10R) is confirmed falls from 0.44 at K 16 to 0.36 at K 30.

Correlated luck grows with K. Day-30 expected false passes among all-null traders are 0.07 (K 16) vs 0.11 (K 30) at rho 0.3, and 0.19 vs 0.24 at rho 0.6. Merging duplicates is what keeps rho near the low end.

Budget: verified cost model. 30 traders fit $500 only with ignore-new-signals plus event-only hold checks (P3-ignore $282-361 at the p90 day), which removes the switch-up lever and the hold management the owners want. 10-20 traders fit with switch calls and P2/P3 checks. Scaling the verified per-trader figures ($19-26/trader-month on the draft P4+switch plan, $9-12 on P3-ignore), 16 traders with switch-up and event checks plus 3 twins plus about $55 analyst/coach should land at about $250-420/month. That leaves room for the 3x thinking-token uncertainty and the burst cache-miss risk (about +$280/month at 30 traders without a pre-warm). Measure it in wave 0.
Operational load and lock discipline: 16 prompts, cards and coin-flip pools are the most that can be built and tested by 10/16.

november_promotion_rule.principle: Day-30 data are used only to stop traders for futility, never to promote one. Rankings do not carry between runs (Spearman -0.13 v3a vs later), live cell spread is 10x the 5y spread, and a 30-day verdict sees only edges of about 0.3R or more.
november_promotion_rule.day30_checks: 11/16 for wave 1, 11/30 for wave 2. AI calls stop (futility) if (a) the 1%-risk R curve is at -15% or worse, or (b) there are >= 30 trades and the day-clustered 90% upper bound of mean R is < 0 (design 10-3 fail rule). By sel/loss.py, (a) by day 30 catches 69% of zero-skill traders (net -0.17R; median day 23), 4% at net +0.05R and 1% at net +0.10R. A stopped trader keeps its rule account (2/2s), signal tracking and coin flips at cost 0, and it stays in K as a non-pass.
november_promotion_rule.global_futility: At 11/16, if the pooled paired AI-minus-rule difference on the same signals (design 10-5 (a), day clusters) has a 90% upper bound < 0 and a point estimate <= -0.05R, stop all AI calls. Rule tracking continues.
november_promotion_rule.what_promotion_can_mean: (1) A surviving trader just continues; nothing is added to the 12/31 family after 11/01. (2) A rule-only strategy can be promoted only into an edition-2 pre-registration (start <= 1/1, 2027 candidate) by criteria fixed now: 5y gross >= 0 in both halves, >= 10 signals/day in AI scope, not a merged duplicate, and every-signal replay mean (4h clusters) not below -(cost + 0.1R). Never on account P&L or leaderboards. (3) Budget freed by futility stops is not used for new judged traders (K is fixed). It may keep Opus twins of survivors running.
november_promotion_rule.real_money: Only a trader that passes the 12/31 verdict (below), and still at 1% risk per stop.

exposure_caps.why: 52% of core every-signal rows share coin, bar and side with another strategy, and in the 15m replay 2,255 signal-accounts were only 1,152 distinct entries. Overlapping traders hold the same position, so 1% each becomes 3-5% on one event (sizing verifier). Caps also stop five traders passing together on one trending month.
exposure_caps.per_coin_direction: At most 3 concurrent AI positions on the same coin and side across all 16 traders (3R at 1% risk).
exposure_caps.per_same_bet_cluster: At most 1 concurrent position per coin-side inside each same-bet cluster: Supertrend {N23_HA_ST, DOGE}; DeepSeek trend {F7_RF_TRIPLE, F4_FAN, F6_VWAP_CROSS}; pullback {F16_FIB382, F9_FVG}. These are the clusters whose live signals fall in the same coin-side 4h window >= 80% of the time, or that are the same entry idea.
exposure_caps.book_direction: At most 8 concurrent same-direction AI positions across all coins (the 6 coins move together, so long BTC plus long ETH is close to one bet).
exposure_caps.tie_break: Pre-registered: widest stop first (lowest cost in R, +0.014R free), then a fixed daily rotation of trader IDs. Never by confidence or recent results.
exposure_caps.logging: Each cap-blocked entry is logged as REJECTED_CAP with its shadow outcome. The coin flip copies realised entries, so caps do not bias the coin-flip test. A trader blocked on >20% of intended entries is flagged in the verdict report.
exposure_caps.coins: All 6 coins allowed. At 1% risk the notional is small, so BCH/LTC book-walk costs mostly vanish (C6), but BCH then LTC go last in ties. 4h entries only after the per-signal 20x liquidation check (5y: 8.1% of 4h signals at 20x liquidate before the 2 ATR stop).

loss_limits.risk_per_stop: Flat 1% for judged traders. Leverage is a code output (the highest of 50/40/30/20x at which stop + buffer sits inside liquidation, floor 3x per design 4-3). Confidence 2-5% sizing only in a non-judged twin until confidence is shown informative (>= 200 trades, Spearman > 0). Basis: at today's cost, 1% at gross 0 halves the account in ~46% of paths by 12/31 and 2% in ~79% (sizing verifier). The verdict is in R either way.
loss_limits.daily: -3R per trader per KST day (09:00 reset): no new entries that day. Simulated hit rate: 15% of days for a zero-skill trader, 6% for a net +0.10R trader (sel/loss.py, 4 trades/day). Coin flips apply the same rule.
loss_limits.trader_review: -15% on the 1% R curve (about -16R) is a pre-registered futility stop of AI calls, not a pause-and-restart. Hit by 12/31: 99% of zero-skill traders, 33% at net 0, 11% at +0.05R, 2% at +0.10R.
loss_limits.book: If the 16 traders together are at <= -12R realised plus unrealised in one KST day, no new AI entries until 09:00 (correlated crash days: per-trader crash losses under risk sizing were single digits to ~20%, Z7).
loss_limits.existing: Keep the design risk rules: 3 losses -> 1h cooldown; no re-entry on the same coin and side for 2 own bars after a loss; macro-event entry blackout; bankrupt line 1,000 USDT; stop placed the moment a lock arms (C11).

verdict_and_multiple_testing.family: One BH family of K = 16 Sonnet traders (fixed at wave-2 launch, counting futility-stopped and too-few-trade traders as non-passes), q = 0.05, one-sided p against the design 10,000 matched coin flips. Opus twins, H3A rule record, exploratory and rule-only accounts are outside it. Rule (2/2s) family: judge only cells with a custom value adopted through the 5y gate before D0 plus the 16 portfolio strategies' 2s, also q 0.05. The other ~180 rule cells are monitoring only, so the second family keeps some power.
verdict_and_multiple_testing.thresholds: Rank i needs p <= 0.05*i/16: 0.0031, 0.0063, 0.0094, ... (z >= 2.73 for a lone discovery).
verdict_and_multiple_testing.minimum_trades: >= 100 resolved trades in the judged window and >= 40 in each half. Below that: insufficient (still counted in K). The design's 30-trade minimum lets a pass rest on an excess of about 0.5R over the coin flip in 30 trades, which is a streak.
verdict_and_multiple_testing.recommended_window: Single pre-registered window: D0 -> 12/26 09:00 KST (wave 1 ~70 days, ~280 trades at 4/day; wave 2 ~56 days, ~220 trades). Pass = BH pass AND mean R > 0 AND mean R > 0 in each half AND still > 0 without the top 5% of trades AND 1%-curve DD <= 25% AND excess > 0 against the paired side-flip and the same-side random-time baselines (sign only; LF5). Day 30 is a futility look only.
verdict_and_multiple_testing.power: 80% power needs an excess over the coin flip of (2.73+0.84)*sd/sqrt(n): n 280 -> 0.21R (net about +0.06R at 0.15R blended cost), n 220 -> 0.24R (net +0.09R), n 100 -> 0.36R, n 84 (H3A-like 1h trader) -> 0.39R. In sel/sim2.py (sd 1.0R, rho 0.3), one true trader at net +0.05 / +0.10 / +0.15R passes with probability 0.52 / 0.78 / 0.93 in wave 1 and 0.45 / 0.71 / 0.88 in wave 2. A low-frequency 1h trader at net +0.13R passes with ~0.33.
verdict_and_multiple_testing.if_owners_keep_two_stage_design: Day-30 pass then a separate days 31-60 pass. Power for the same net +0.10R trader is about 0.44 at K 16 (sel/sim.py). False passes are lower: about 0.002-0.005. Never act on day-30 passes: expected false day-30 passes are 0.06-0.19 at K 16 (rho 0-0.6).

expected_false_passes.rule_family: At most about 0.05 if judged by BH. In practice about 0, because default rules sit at -cost.
expected_false_passes.project: Nominal project alpha = rule bot 0.10 + AI bot 0.10 (design 10-2). State this on the first line of the 12/31 report.
expected_false_passes.p_at_least_one_pass: If no trader has a real edge (the evidence-based default), P(>= 1 pass) is just the false-pass rate, about 0.02-0.03. If exactly one trader nets +0.10R/trade: about 0.71-0.78 (single window) or 0.44 (two-stage). With an assumed 3% per-trader chance of such an edge (an assumption, not a measurement): expected true passes about 16 x 0.03 x 0.75 = 0.36.

design_implications: Lock K = 16 and the wave-2 list before 10/17; record the actual count at each wave start; futility-stopped traders stay in K.

Replace or supplement the 30-trade, two-stage day-30/day-60 verdict with the single 12/26 window above (owner decisions D1/D3/D21 are still open). If the two-stage version is kept, write into the verdict code that day-30 passes trigger nothing.
Raise the minimum to >= 100 trades per judged window (>= 40 per half) and print the MDE beside every verdict (design 10-7).
Judged traders use flat 1% risk per stop. Leverage is chosen by code from the stop. Exits are in R/price (the ROE ladder converted at 20x geometry, as design 3-4 already does).
Put the cross-trader caps (coin-side 3, cluster 1, book direction 8) and the book daily stop (-12R) in the risk manager. Log REJECTED_CAP with shadows; the tie-break is widest stop first.

Hold policy: ignore same-tf and lower-tf signals while holding; wake on higher-tf own signals, opposite signals on the held coin, a 1.0R move (15-minute cooldown) and macro events. Routine held-tf bar-close checks go to the small model. This keeps 16 traders well inside $500 and keeps the switch-up lever.
Timeframe scope per trader follows its 5y gross sign (e.g. S4 without 15m, F16 without 30m, N25 without 30m). This is a pre-registered card field, not an AI choice.
Weekly custom-value search is a record only. Adoption needs the money unit (net % per notional) and a z threshold that accounts for best-of-225 (about 3.5), so expect no adoption before 12/31.
Fix the coin-flip pool (same run and tf vs same coin) in the verdict code before D0. N17-type timing results moved from +0.39 to +0.52 between pool definitions.

Log every signal each trader saw with its take/skip decision and the same-moment rule replay. The paired AI-minus-rule test (design 10-5 (a)) is the most powerful test of whether the AI adds anything, and it drives global futility.

H3A needs a limit-fill engine and an L/S ratio feed by 10/30. Its one-position AI version is a different experiment from the 5y multi-position result, so keep the multi-position cost-free record alongside it.
Pre-register edition 2 (D07 liquidations, D05 funding-trend after a 5y test, promoted rule strategies) in November. Nothing new enters edition 1 after 11/01.
Wave 0 must measure tokens with usage fields (count_tokens is free), cache writes for the Opus twins, and the 20-second deadline with max_retries set. Late answers are billed.
what_would_change_my_mind: Wave-0 blind replay shows the AI separates signals: skipped-minus-taken >= +0.15R over >= 300 replayed decisions with day clusters. That raises the prior, and I would expand toward 20-24 traders using the reserves (N09_ALLIG_AROON, N02_ST_KST, N12_ICHI_AO) if the budget allows.
A measured cost under ~$8/trader-month with switch-up and event checks removes the budget argument. The duplicate and anti-edge arguments still cap distinct seats at about 18-20.
If a 5y entry-level overlap check shows F16_FIB382 and F9_FVG share > 50% of entries (or DOGE and N23 > 50%), merge them and free a seat for N09.
If the H3A build is ready and its multi-position record tracks the 5y +0.2%/trade through October, I would weight it as the lead candidate. If its feed is unreliable, it drops out.
Day-30 pooled AI-minus-rule <= -0.05R with the CI below 0: stop the AI cohort (global futility).
A volatility regime change (stops back to 5y-typical widths) cuts the cost in R by ~1.5x (hurdle about 0.15R at 15m), which makes 15m-led traders less hopeless. It does not change who is staffed.
A pre-registered 5y test of D05 or D04 (catalog rule exactly) that passes both halves would justify a new-information seat in edition 2.
honest_warnings: No strategy beats a coin flip before costs on live data, and on 5 years the best 15m gross (+0.026R) is about 1/9 of the 0.23R cost. These 16 are the least-bad, non-duplicate, frequent bets. They are not good strategies.

The likeliest 12/31 result is "no trader passes". With zero AI edge, the chance of any pass is about 2-3%, and if one appears it should be treated as possibly false until small real money confirms it.
Every staffed trader at -cost loses about 0.6-0.8R a day. About 70% are expected to hit the -15% futility stop by day 30.
Wave 2 has less time (~56 days) and the 1h-led or session traders (H3A, F15_ASIA_BRK, N13, S4) have low power. Their inclusion mostly buys a chance, not a likely verdict.
DeepSeek-based passes (F16, F9, F7, F6, F4_FAN, F15) stay preliminary until the DeepSeek FORWARD_PREREG J1 (2027-02-02).
Overlap clusters come from 4.8 live days of signal_log (sel/ovl.py). 4h-window overlap is inflated for very busy strategies, and 5y entry-level overlap was not computed.

The power and false-pass numbers come from simple simulations (sd 1.0R, ~4 trades/day, blended cost 0.15R, equicorrelation rho). Real R tails are heavier and costs at 15m are 0.23R, so treat them as order-of-magnitude.
Paper still flatters real execution: LTC/BCH/DOGE half-spread is not in slip_best, 41% of v4 stop-slip rows were never measured, and mark-price liquidation is not modelled.

Caps, futility stops and the single-window verdict change design v2 decisions that are still open (D1, D3, D10, D21). They need the owners' explicit yes before 10/17, and nothing about them may change after D0.
